verdict.rationale: Morph documents running production agents, including Claude Code over its native Anthropic Messages endpoint, on its open-weight models such as Kimi K3, which implies working agent tool loops. However, no evidence explicitly documents function/tool-calling support, its fidelity, or parallel tool calls. Missing for 10: explicit tool/function-calling documentation, parallel tool call support, multi-step tool-use reliability evidence, independent hands-on corroboration of agent loops on open models.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on faithful function/tool calling — including parallel and multi-step tool use — so agent loops run on open models without breaking

citations.quote: Move a production agent off Anthropic or OpenAI onto Kimi K3 — a 5% traffic trial or a full migration, gated by Reflexes.
Claude Code speaks the Anthropic Messages API, which Morph serves natively at `/v1/messages`.
Anthropic Messages supports the same open source chat models, token billing, and rate limits.
